recognize_zh: 這顆嗜中性球的核只分成兩個圓形核葉、以細絲相連（夾鼻眼鏡狀，pince-nez），染色質粗塊狀聚集，細胞質淡而顆粒稀少，符合假性 Pelger-Huët（Pelgeroid）變化。
features: Mature-sized neutrophil with bilobed nucleus: two round lobes joined by a thin chromatin strand (pince-nez configuration)
Pale cytoplasm with markedly reduced specific granules (hypogranularity)
Background erythrocytes unremarkable; a single platelet nearby
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a neutrophil with a hyposegmented bilobed nucleus in a pince-nez configuration, coarse chromatin clumping and pale, hypogranular cytoplasm. Red cells in the field show no significant abnormality. In an acquired setting, these findings are consistent with pseudo-Pelger-Huët (Pelgeroid) change, a dysgranulopoietic feature that should prompt evaluation for a myelodysplastic neoplasm or drug effect.

ddx.vs: Inherited LBR-related anomaly affects nearly all neutrophils uniformly with normal granulation, whereas pseudo-Pelger cells are a subpopulation often accompanied by hypogranularity and other dysplasia.
Band forms have a continuous U-shaped nucleus of uniform width without a thin filament separating discrete round lobes, and granulation is normal.

ddx.dx: Drug-induced Pelgeroid change (e.g., mycophenolate, tacrolimus, valproate)
ddx.vs: Morphology can be identical; clinical drug history and resolution after withdrawal distinguish it from MDS.
Eosinophils are also typically bilobed but contain abundant large orange-red granules rather than pale agranular cytoplasm.
